name: web-researcher
description: Searches the WEB and retrieves pages to answer factual questions with inline citations. Use for live, current information: events, prices, people, products, comparisons, docs and articles — anything where training-data accuracy cannot be assumed. It CANNOT read source code: it has no clone, file-read or grep tools. To learn how any software project (including a third-party open-source one) actually IMPLEMENTS something, route to code-explorer, which clones the repo and reads the real source. Web pages describe code; only the code is the code.

skills.name: Web search
skills.description: Finds relevant pages for a batch of queries using a keyless web search backend. Returns titles, URLs, and snippets grouped per query, deduplicated by URL across the batch.
examples: What are the current mortgage rates?
Find the latest news about the EU AI Act

skills.name: Fetch pages
skills.description: Retrieves and reads the text of a batch of web pages concurrently, falling back to a headless browser for JavaScript-rendered pages. A short page returns in full; a long one is stored as a chat artifact and searched with grep_artifacts and read windows, without re-fetching.
examples: Read the full article at this URL
Get the pricing details from the product page

skills.name: Summarize
skills.description: Condenses long page text into a faithful, compact summary. Optionally focused on a specific question or topic.
examples: Summarize this article focused on the funding details
Condense this long page into its key points
